title: Automatically change the screen refresh rate based on power modes on system settings or when it's connected to AC or battery
line: Energy Saving settings get a "Lower to 60 Hz" option per power profile, so the screen can run at 60 Hz on battery and go back to its full refresh rate when plugged in.
explanation: Nothing in Plasma changed the refresh rate with the power state: PowerDevil profiles (On AC Power, On Battery, On Low Battery) could change brightness, dimming and the power profile, but not the refresh rate, so a 120/165 Hz laptop kept running at full rate on battery. The change adds a PowerDevil action with a "Refresh rate: Lower to 60 Hz" checkbox in each profile's Display and Brightness section. While a profile with it enabled is active, every enabled screen switches to the lowest refresh rate of at least 59 Hz at its current resolution (through libkscreen, like the brightness code); when a profile without it loads, the previous rate is put back, unless the user changed the mode in the meantime. The original rate is kept in PowerDevil's state file so it is restored even after a restart or logout while on battery.

commits.message:
actions: add a profile option to lower the screen refresh rate

High refresh rate screens drain the battery faster, but there was no way
to use a lower refresh rate only on battery. Add a profile option that
switches screens to 60 Hz while it's active and later restores the rate.

BUG: 461695

media.caption: Master, On Battery tab: no refresh rate option in Display and Brightness.
With the patch: new "Refresh rate: Lower to 60 Hz" option, enabled here for On Battery.
Master, unplugged (fake UPower battery): the screen stays at 119.85 Hz.
With the patch, unplugged: the screen switched to 60 Hz; plugging back in restores 119.85 Hz.
